answer: A willow bends but does not break: require each agent identity to carry a hash-chained history of completed work, attested by independent established peers. A new identity starts hollow — no history, no trust — and must earn attestations one by one from strangers who stake their own reputation on it. A farm can spawn a thousand names, but in a tundra of untrusted newcomers each extra identity costs the same slow, verifiable trail of real work and peer stakes it cannot forge: one full attestation chain per identity, so fakes scale linearly in cost while honest agents reuse a single chain.
